title: save/fight.js serialises live SoulsAI as plain object; boot-check blind to it
next_step: none — piece complete; a critic should judge it (rule 22)
notes: combat/ai.js and combat/enemy.js are declared by W1-12 [done] and W1-03 [fixed]; neither is building and both files were clean in the working tree when claimed. Declared here rather than left to read as a collision (rule 16).
NOT touching game/src/engine.js: 8 live pieces, working tree MM (staged AND unstaged neighbour edits). A `git commit --only game/src/engine.js` would carry them.

PRE-FIX REPRODUCTION (commit 63f41ef + working tree, one browser): ctl.ai constructor SoulsAI -> Object across saveRoundTrip(); ai.step is not a function on the next stepFrames(1); hash_equal false; the serialised SoulsAI is 81,892 of the 194,161-byte save (42%) because it drags the whole CombatBody, statblock and ai.json along with it.

SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND, NOT MINE TO FIX: game/src/engine.js:7182 nulls this.death.lastGrounded on every load where the death surface is not active, one statement after DeathSystem.restoreInFlight() restored it -- so death.last_grounded is the OTHER half of hash_equal:false and the D3 fall-rule respawn point does not survive a load. Same family as the comment four lines above it. Handed up.

FLEET NOTE: at the start of this run the whole tree was unbootable (Engine._installCanon threw on 2 unresolved canon refs after bank 63f41ef swept W1-17's in-flight removal of the `notary` infos). Someone demoted the throw to a warning mid-run and boot-check went green again. Not my change.

RULE 17 / SWEEPING, reported rather than diagnosed as a neighbour: commit 692b6aa ('S37: the corpus governs dialogue selection and the engine yields') carried my in-flight game/src/save/fight.js, game/src/combat/ai.js, game/src/combat/enemy.js, tools/check-save-shape.mjs and tools/check-data.mjs under its own message, along with many other agents' files. I did not intend that and I am recording it rather than trying to unpick it. `git commit --only` with paths that are already committed does NOT restrict the commit to nothing; see dd63f6c, where another agent recorded the same thing ('record that --only did not fully hold').

TREE RED TWICE DURING THIS RUN, neither mine, both rule 13: (1) Engine._installCanon threw on 2 unresolved canon refs after bank 63f41ef swept W1-17's removal of the `notary` infos -- someone demoted it to a warning mid-run; (2) converse.js orderTopicDocs threw because game/data/dialogue/topics/_manifest.json exists on disk but was not listed in game/data/index.json, so the engine loaded 21 grouped topic docs without it. Both blocked all browser work for the whole box while they lasted.

CONTENTION: `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` returned GO before each browser run (2 instances / room for 4, then room for 3). Five browser runs total: one pre-fix diagnostic, one post-fix diagnostic, three boot-check runs (fixed, pre-fix, naive-SKIP), plus timing and the three consumption arms. Own browser used throughout rather than tools/capture/, because every measurement here steps the simulation (RULES 20).
The screenshot was taken with my own browser for the same reason: the frame only means anything after a save, a load and 240 fixed steps.

fix.what: save/fight.js now classifies every actor field: a LIVE OBJECT (class instance) is carried through its own saveState()/loadState() -- the contract Rig already had in combat/skeleton.js -- or it is not carried at all and is named in __unsaved. loadActor never assigns a plain object over a live one. SoulsAI grew saveState/loadState with an explicit MACHINERY set (b, stat, cfg, A, omega, sightR, walk, sprint, leashHard -- all pure functions of the statblock and ai.json, all rebuilt by the constructor) and an AI_FRAME_STAMPS set so its nine clocks are rebased like the body's. EnemyController._resolveAI() re-resolves when behaviour is 'souls' but ai is null, which is the load path.
fix.why_not_SKIP: EnemyController._idleBehaviour() guards its whole souls branch with `if (this.ai)`, so adding `ai` to SKIP would have restored it as null and the enemy would stop thinking without throwing -- the quieter, worse half of the same defect. Same shape as `post` in save/state.js.

measured_after.hash_equal_residual: death.last_grounded ONLY -- engine.js:7182, not this piece's file

commit_of_fix: 692b6aa (a neighbour commit swept the source files before my own; see below) + be9af27/674c107

boot_check_extension.what: boot-check.mjs now spawns one guard_legion, steps once to build its AI, saveState -> structural clone -> loadState, and steps again. Armed (STRICT_STEP) only after being shown silent and able to fail.
boot_check_extension.cost: 622 ms added. saveRoundTrip() was tried first and cost 3,110 ms -- two extra getStateHash() calls and a stateDiff the arm does not need -- so it was replaced with saveState/clone/loadState. 900 ms of the remaining 622-1100 ms is loadState() rebuilding the world, which is the thing under test.
proven_red_two_ways: against the real pre-fix source served from a scratch copy: rendered_a_frame TRUE, harness_responsive TRUE, stepped_after_a_load FALSE, step_error 'this.ai.step is not a function', exit 12. Every pre-existing arm of boot-check stayed green, which is the point.

against the NAIVE fix (ai added to SKIP), which throws nothing at all: step_error 'a live AI was lost across the round trip: 2 before, 0 after', exit 12. The arm counts live AIs rather than only watching for an exception, so the silent variant is caught too.
boot_check_extension.quiet_where_it_cannot_know: no verbs / no combat state / no live AI on the floor -> stepped_after_a_load is null and the gate ignores it.

consumption_RI_MTH07.world_side_consumer: EnemyController._idleBehaviour() -> SoulsAI.step(), which writes b.pos/b.yaw/b.state/b.speedMps and emits enemy_state. The leash test (T25) is the FIRST decision step() takes and it reads this.anchor, which exists nowhere but on the AI.
consumption_RI_MTH07.B_perturbed_anchor: saved anchor moved 300 m; restored body enters LEASH_RETURN and walks 8.672 m to (2765.368, 5006.868)
consumption_RI_MTH07.C_null_control: perturbed ai.s.yawRate (a trace output assigned every frame before anything reads it) -> byte-identical to A, 0.000 m. So B is not noise.
consumption_RI_MTH07.D_delete_the_fix: same script against a served copy of the pre-fix source: fixture sound (ai_live_before_save true), then 'the AI came back without step()', exit 2. The teardown bites.
consumption_RI_MTH07.which_shape: a single fix, not two guards and not an inert one: cutting it alone returns the old failure.

hash_equal.fight_enemies_cause: moveKeyOf() resolves a move object to its TABLE KEY by identity (table[k] === m). Nested under ctl.ai.b.moves the save carried COPIES, so on re-save identity failed and moveKeyOf fell back to m.id -- 'roll' where the first save wrote 'roll_LIGHT'. Gone with the ai subtree.
hash_equal.residual_NOT_MINE: game/src/engine.js:7182 -- `if (this.death.active) ... else { this.death.lastHp = null; this.death.lastGrounded = null; }` runs on every load, one statement after DeathSystem.restoreInFlight() restored lastGrounded from the blob. save/state.js:336 writes it, death.js:98 reads it back, and this line then throws it away. It is the D3 fall-rule respawn point, so a player who loads a save loses where they last stood on solid ground. Exactly the shape of the comment four lines above it. NOT FIXED: engine.js has 8 live claimants and was `MM` (staged AND unstaged neighbour edits) throughout, so `git commit --only game/src/engine.js` would have carried them.

'It took two runs of my probe down before I stepped one frame at a time and cleared hostiles around it.' Two probe runs lost, and the figures that survived were taken with hostiles cleared out of the way.

No worktree-level delete-the-fix of the boot-check change itself; the delete-the-fix was done at the source level (a served scratch copy of the pre-fix game/) which is stronger, but it means the arms were run on a COPY of game/, not on the shared tree.

getDurableFieldCensus() was not extended to walk enemy controllers (it only calls saveActor on bodies and playerCtl), so the census still cannot see an enemy ctl field going missing. Named, not fixed.
The `__unsaved` list is written by saveActor and read by check-save-shape, but nothing surfaces it in getSaveManifest()'s path census; on a sound tree it is absent so this costs nothing today.
No judgement of my own work (RULES 22) — a critic with fresh context is needed.
